destination.name: Daintree
destination.tagline: Ancient World Heritage rainforest that meets the Great Barrier Reef at the shore
destination.description: The Daintree is a tropical rainforest in Far North Queensland, thought to be over 135 million years old and part of the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area. It is one of the few places where two World Heritage sites, the rainforest and the Great Barrier Reef, meet. Visitors cross the Daintree River by ferry to reach Cape Tribulation and its beaches, boardwalks and wildlife. The cassowary is its icon, alongside about 430 bird species.

goodToKnow.title: Cross the river by ferry
goodToKnow.detail: Cape Tribulation lies north of the Daintree River, which you cross by ferry. Allow time for the crossing when planning your day.

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles and stingers
goodToKnow.detail: Crocodiles live in the river, creeks and sea, and stingers are present in summer. Stay away from the shore and never swim at night.

goodToKnow.title: Avoid the wet season
goodToKnow.detail: November to March is the rainy and cyclone season. Check road conditions before heading north of the river.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the drier months, easier for walking. Nov–Mar is the rainy and cyclone season.
